description: Table 1 is a purely tabular figure (chart_table): a single ruled grid of text with no micrographs, curves, maps or schematics. Its caption reads "Table 1. Chemical content of experimental raw materials (mass percentage, %)", with footnote a) defined as representing trace amounts. The grid has a header row of seven composition columns — C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ti, Al — and three data rows naming the raw materials: Iron powder, Ferromanganese and Aluminum particles. Iron powder reports C 0.35, Si 0.01, Mn 0.046, P 0.022, S 0.013, Ti 0.0086, with Al given as "–". Ferromanganese reports C 0.76, Si 1.46, Mn 65.860, S 0.032, with P, Ti and Al given as "–"; 65.860 is by far the largest value in the table, confirming ferromanganese as the manganese carrier. Aluminum particles report Al 99.999 with all other elements "–", except C, whose cell is a superscripted a) footnote mark, i.e. trace amount. Hyphens "–" therefore denote elements not reported/not present. The table specifies the charge used to melt the Fe-15Mn-xAl-C (x = 1, 3, 5) low-density steels: baseline carbon comes from iron powder, Mn from ferromanganese, and Al from 99.999% aluminium particles.

observations.observation: The figure is a table with a header row of seven chemical symbols: C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ti, Al, under a first column headed 'Raw material'.
The table lists exactly three raw materials as rows: 'Iron powder', 'Ferromanganese' and 'Aluminum particles'.
Iron powder row values are C 0.35, Si 0.01, Mn 0.046, P 0.022, S 0.013, Ti 0.0086, and Al is given as a dash '–'.
Ferromanganese row values are C 0.76, Si 1.46, Mn 65.860, S 0.032, while P, Ti and Al are each given as '–'.
The largest number printed anywhere in the table is the Mn content of ferromanganese, 65.860, making ferromanganese the manganese carrier of the charge.
Aluminum particles row gives Al = 99.999 while every other element cell in that row is '–' except C, which carries a superscript a) footnote mark.
The caption defines the superscript a) as representing trace amounts, so the C cell of the aluminum-particles row means a trace C content rather than a measured value.
The caption states the table gives chemical content of experimental raw materials in mass percentage (%).
Dash entries '–' are used consistently for elements not reported for a given raw material (e.g. Al in iron powder and ferromanganese).
